# Introduction

SeuratSourcery provides a lightweight and reproducible framework for
loading, validating, harmonizing and inspecting single-cell datasets
before integration.

Key issues found between datasets for these analyses include: -
Mismatched gene symbols - Missing layers - Duplicated cells - Different
sized data

SeuratSourcery packages together a toolbox for dealing with these issues
allowing for a quick and easy visualization of the characteristics of
the dataset

This vignette goes through: Loading toy datasets, harmonizing assays,
inspecting dataset properties, generating a sourcery report

# Installation

You can install the development version from GitHub:

```{r eval=FALSE}
require("devtools")
install_github("josephDURAISINGH/SeuratSourcery")
devtools::load_all()

```

Optional dependencies for H5AD and H5Seurat support:

```{r}
# IF BIOMANAGER ISN'T INSTALLED PLEASE DO SO FOR THIS FUNCTIONALITY
# if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
#   install.packages("BiocManager")
# 
# BiocManager::install(c("zellkonverter", "HDF5Array", "DelayedArray"))
```

Quickstart Example 1. Load packages Writing

```{r}
library(SeuratSourcery)
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
```

2.  Pull our mock data. Mock data was used for lightweight
    representation of a single cell dataset This can be a list of your
    own singlecell file paths, or a directory that contains them

Writing

```{r}
demo_dir <- system.file("extdata/demo_datasets", package = "SeuratSourcery")
if (dir.exists(demo_dir)) {
   runes <- summonData(demo_dir)
   print(names(runes))
}
```

3.  Inspect and visualize An output of the first set of plots. These
    plots and tables give a variety of metrics with useful information
    between the datasets. This information can be used to guide
    downstream analysis of the data as well as dataset level analysis An
    example of this is seeing which dataset has more cells, more genes
    Or how much of

```{r}
report1 <- runeInspection(runes)
getSourceryReport(report1, show_plot = FALSE)
```

4.  Harmonize datasets This standardizes gene identifiers, metadata
    names, and other conventions to assure compatibility The demo data
    is very clean so there will be little to no affect of the
    harmonization in the demo When using your own data this will do
    things

```{r}
runes_harmonized <- activateRune(runes)
```

5.  Inspect and visualize Some cases the harmonization will change the
    values, so by running the visualization before and after, we can be
    informed on how the datasets have been affected. Writing

```{r}
report <- runeInspection(runes_harmonized)
getSourceryReport(report, show_plot = FALSE)
```

Rune inspection calculates some key metrics about the dataset. These
include the number of genes, features, overlapping genes between
datasets and more. getSourceryReport produces summary tables and plots
showing dataset sizes, gene overlaps, and metadata coverage.

6.  Downstream analysis The integrated object can then be used in
    standard Seurat downstream workflows (e.g., PCA, clustering,
    visualization). Although this is not included in this package (see
    <https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/integration_introduction> for
    more info on this). By inputting

1b. Full pipeline (one-liner) Alternatively, this combines loading,
harmonization and inspection into a single easy step. Point the path to
dataset or feed in the group of datasets directly under the datasets =
parameter Small chance of hitting a bug in which case running
devtools::load_all() has been known to fix it

Writing

```{r eval=FALSE}
demo_dir <- system.file("extdata/demo_datasets", package = "SeuratSourcery")
print(demo_dir)
final_obj <- performSourcery(path = demo_dir)
```

1c. Shiny App To launch Shiny app use the following function to get real
time visualizations Upload the datasets, multiselect all of the files
you want to compare and summon data - Example: Browse to
extdata/demo_datasets and then shift select demo_A to demo_C Then
activate runes (even without any checked boxes) Then click update
sourcery report and select the plots you would like to see! Note: Shiny
not compatible with folders and by extension 10x data in this version

```{r, eval=FALSE}
runSeuratSourcery()
```
